before: A C program is instructions written as source text. A compiler translates the text into a program that can run. This course shows code, but does not compile C in the browser.
#include <stdio.h> makes declarations for standard input and output functions available. It is a preprocessing directive, not an output command.
int main(void) starts our program definition. main is the entry function in this hosted example; void here means it takes no parameters. Braces group its body.
puts("Hello"); calls a library function with quoted text and prints it followed by a newline. A semicolon ends the statement.
return 0; ends main and reports successful completion to its environment. It is not a command to print zero. Statements before it execute in order.
after: A program is a set of instructions a computer follows. C is a language for writing those instructions. A compiler turns your C text into a program the computer can run.
`#include <stdio.h>` brings in information about ready-made tools for reading and printing. It lets the compiler recognize the printing tool used below.
A function is a named piece of work. `main` is where this program starts. In `int main(void)`, `void` means no inputs. The braces hold its instructions.
`puts` prints the text inside its parentheses, then starts a new line. Quotes mark the text. The semicolon ends the instruction.
`return 0;` ends main and reports that the program finished successfully. It does not print 0. The printing instructions run in their written order.

before: Read one idea at a time.
Apply the idea to the changed situation.
Trace the values and instructions in their execution order.
after: Follow the two puts lines from top to bottom.

before.question: If puts("Compass"); moves before puts("Map");, what prints first?
choices: Compass, because it now executes first.
before.explanation: The first puts call displays Compass; returning 0 is a status, not printed text.

after.question: If the Compass line comes before the Map line, what prints first?
choices: Compass, because its instruction comes first.
Map, because C sorts the words.
after.explanation: The computer follows the puts instructions in order. Moving the Compass line first makes Compass print first.
